rationale.conceptual: The method involves a specific, multi-component theoretical framework (tight-binding, exciton transformation, coupled Bloch equations) that demands understanding of semiconductor quantum optics and computational physics. It is not a standard library call but a custom implementation requiring translation of non-trivial many-body equations into code.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of ~4 sequential stages (band structure, exciton wave function, spectra computation, weight extraction) with interdependent data. While not extremely long, it requires careful handling of numerical solvers and parameter sweeps over three nanotubes and many temperatures, typical of a multi-stage computational physics workflow.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies a non-trivial many-body density matrix approach with excitonic wave functions and coupled equations to compute exciton-phonon sidebands in carbon nanotubes. Implementing this requires substantial theoretical physics understanding, coding of tight-binding band structures, Coulomb matrix elements, exciton wave functions, and solving integro-differential equations. The pipeline has multiple stages but is manageable in scope. Resource needs are modest, entirely CPU-based with low data volumes.

compute_estimate.reasoning: One-dimensional tight-binding model with low numbers of nanotubes (3) and phonon modes; computations are CPU-bound with modest memory requirements (matrix sizes small, frequency grid moderate). No large datasets needed.
